messages:
Priya: Heads-up — customer on dedicated pool dp-acme-3 opened an escalation. Since 02:10 UTC their p95 token throughput dropped ~60% and end-to-end latency jumped. No obvious 5xx spike but many short responses and increased tail latency.

Priya: Quick observables 
- continuous_batcher.avg_batch_size: 1.2 (was ~6.8 baseline)
- prefill_queue_depth: low (~0.3) but scheduler_pending backlog ~110
- gpu_util: 32%
- tokens/sec: down 58%

infra-bot: auto-alert: dedicated-pool/dp-acme-3 throughput-anomaly at 2025-08-12T02:12:00Z. Relevant metrics: {"cb.avg_batch":1.2, "prefill.depth":0.33, "sched.pending":112} :warning:

Leo: Hypothesis: continuous-batcher is producing tiny micro-batches (avg ~1) -> inefficient kernel utilization -> throughput drop. Suspect noisy tenant(s) causing frequent prefill eviction or high-prefill variance so scheduler keeps draining single-request packs. Autoscale didn't trigger because GPU util stayed low.

Ava: Can you dump recent scheduler events and the batcher decisions? If max_batch_tokens was accidentally reduced in a recent config roll that would fragment packs. Also check if per-tenant rate limits changed.

Priya: Attaching quick log snippet from the host (redacted):
```
2025-08-12T02:09:58.112Z INFO prefill: tenant=acme-shop prefills=1 tokens=32 evicted=false
2025-08-12T02:10:02.427Z DEBUG batcher: packed=1 tokens=48 reason=timer
2025-08-12T02:10:02.428Z DEBUG batcher: schedule_decision=drain_small_pack id=0x7f3a
2025-08-12T02:10:05.003Z WARN scheduler: prefill_miss tenant=acme-shop kv_cache_miss=0.76
```

Maria: I ran a repro with a synthetic loader (400 qps, mix of short/long prompts) against a staging replica and saw the same micro-batching behavior. Increasing the request coalescing window from 6ms -> 20ms pushed avg_batch_size to ~4 and restored tokens/sec to ~85% of baseline.

Leo: That suggests scheduler pacing is too aggressive on drain. Possible root causes:
- a recent change to default prefill timeout/pack drain heuristic (rollout ~2025-08-11 23:40 UTC)
- noisy tenant sending lots of single-short requests that cause timer-driven drains
- kv-cache churn forcing more prefix reads and making coalescing ineffective

Ava: Short mitigation options:
- temporarily route the noisy tenant to separate capacity (dedicated tenant isolation) or rate-limit them at the edge.
- increase coalescing window (quick config) to bias toward larger packs.
- enable pack-retention flag so small packs wait an extra tick before draining.

Priya: Customer asks for quick remediation; they prefer not to be moved. Can we try increasing coalescing window on their pool and flip pack-retention? What are safe values?

Leo: I can push a canary: coalescing_ms from 6 -> 18 and pack_retention=true on one node in dp-acme-3. If stable for 5m we can roll. Watchpoints: p95 latency (should not increase for single-request latency beyond 150ms) and gpu_util (should go up).

infra-bot: runbook note: to change coalescing window:
```
PATCH /admin/pools/dp-acme-3/config
{ "continuous_batcher": { "coalescing_ms": 18, "pack_retention": true } }
```
Requires canary label and 2 approvers.

Maria: I already pushed the canary to node-7 at 02:22 UTC. Early signals: avg_batch_size -> 3.9, tokens/sec -> +42%, p95 latency for single-request increased +20ms. No 5xx.

Priya: Customer reports improved throughput on their side, confirmed ~40% uplift. They still see occasional small spikes.

Ava: Next ops steps:
- keep canary for 15m, then roll to remaining nodes if stable.
- capture a full scheduler_trace and batcher_decisions for 02:00-02:30 window and attach to ticket.
- create a short automation: detect sustained avg_batch_size < 2.0 and auto-increase coalescing_ms by +10ms (capped) as circuit-breaker.

Leo: Longer-term: investigate why autoscale didn't trigger — thresholds relying on GPU util are insufficient when micro-batching reduces throughput without driving util high. We should add a throughput-based autoscale metric (tokens/sec or avg_batch_size proxy). Filing follow-up ticket.

Priya: Thanks. I updated the support ticket with remediation steps and customer OK to roll. Moving to monitoring/observation to verify for next 24h. :thumbsup:

support-bot: Ticket #34218 updated: remediation applied (coalescing_ms=18), customer confirmed partial recovery.

Ava: I'll open the infra PR for the autoscale metric change.

Leo: Will follow up on noisy-tenant detection heuristics.

Priya: Closing loop here — if anyone sees regressions ping me.
